title: Field Strategy
summary: How to work the field effectively: laps, call backs and breaking the day down.
body:
## Working the day in laps

### 1st lap

- The qualifying process
- Get the non-qualifiers out of the way
- Get to know your territory
- **Goal:** 100 doors · speak to 30 people before sector break

### 2nd lap

- Qualifiers and decision makers coming back home after the school run and work
- Focus on positive customers
- Follow the systems
- **Goal:** follow your call back tracker (it saves time) · speak to 40 people

### 3rd lap

- More late qualifiers coming back home
- Keep the intensity: don't get complacent
- Pick more doors if needed
- **Goal:** maximise your call back tracker · get closer to your L.O.A. working for you

### Call backs

- Maximise the day by setting call backs
- Ask for referrals throughout the day
- Visit all call backs
- **Goal:** have 10 call backs as a minimum · extra customers to boost your day

## Why have a strategy in the field?

- Be more planned and organised
- Be prepared for the unexpected, always having a back-up plan
- Deal with challenges and obstacles more easily, more quickly and in a calm manner
- Think clearly and logically about our day
- Work the territory more efficiently and save time
- Increase our work ethic and momentum
- Create more fun in the sector, where everyone feels confident and focused
- Increase our sales and therefore our income

### Tips on working the territory effectively

- Research the territory before leaving the office
- Prepare impacts and tips to support your team for the day
- Plan the maps and pairings (always have a back-up plan)
- Create a SENSE OF URGENCY to the field, to have more time selling
- Prepare our lunch, to save time and money
- Be the first one to leave the office and arrive at the field
- Go the extra mile if needed, especially when we are coaching, to give ourselves more time to sell and coach
- Prepare for the weather: cold, warm, hot, rainy (have an umbrella, waterproof jacket, waterproof boots)
- Mark off the map at the end of the day and plan your next day. Try to stay in the same map for as long as you can

> TIP: The area has been pitched before? This is normal. Adapt your introduction by pre-empting customers' concerns: “You probably saw us a few weeks back?” “You probably spoke to us a few months ago?”

## The call back tracker

A call back tracker is a tool used in the field to help with:

- Working the territory correctly and saving time
- Logging all of our appointments and who we have spoken to or need to go back to later
- Identifying how many people we have spoken to
- Understanding our numbers better and being more logical
- Breaking our day down at the end of the day to see the wins, the patterns and what to improve on the next day

### What to record

- **Your basic details:** where you were working, on what date, and who was your Sector Leader
- **Street names** (use CAPITAL LETTERS) and **house numbers**
- **For each door:** people spoken to, pitched, closed
- **Comments:** the time to call back, the customer's name, the hot spot, something you were talking about, the dog's or cat's name: anything to use as a start-up conversation when you come back later
- **Times:** the time we get to the field, the time we leave the field, the time we have a sector break and how long for, the time we start each lap

### Setting up call backs properly

- Set up a call back to speak to the decision maker
- When setting up a call back be indifferent and casual: “No worries, I will be with your neighbours till around 7:30pm, so if I get a chance, I will catch you both later.”
- Never promise you will be back, as you might get busy. It also creates a natural fear of loss
- Aim to have 10 call backs a day
- Start doing call backs after 7:00pm, to ensure they are back home and we are not wasting time

### Tips

- Fill it in neatly so you can read it
- Record your call backs correctly, with small messages, so you have a great way to start a conversation when you are back later
- Use codes to make your life easier
- Record and log the data properly so you can improve the next day
- Have fun with loads of different games and competitions
- Always have a spare call back tracker, in case your original one gets wet or lost
- Keep your call back tracker so you can re-walk the territory the next day

## Breaking the day down

Breaking your day down is a system that helps you keep your focus for a longer period of time. Analysing your day based on numbers allows you to make logical decisions, rather than reacting emotionally to your day. It allows you to focus on the process, not the results.

### Why?

- Everyone needs to stay focused to hit their goals
- It is easier to stay focused for shorter periods of time than a whole day
- Knowing your Law of Averages allows you to work better every day
- You will learn how to focus on the future, not the past

### How?

- On the front or back of your call back tracker
- Every hour in the field, so you know where you are at
- Every night in the office, so you know what to get coaching on the next day
- Set yourself a goal every hour
- If you don't hit your goal, forget about that hour. Don't carry the total to the next hour
- Every hour is a new hour

| Hour | People spoken to | Short stories | Closes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.30 – 2.30 | ⟦number⟧ | ⟦number⟧ | ⟦number⟧ |
| 2.30 – 3.30 | ⟦number⟧ | ⟦number⟧ | ⟦number⟧ |

title: 3 Types of Days
summary: Early days, steady days and late days, and how to stay logical through each.
body:
## What?

Every day is different, and therefore it is important we learn how to understand different types of days and when the sales happen, to prevent getting frustrated and to develop a strong mindset. The key to becoming a top performer in any campaign is to master working different territories, different customers and different types of days. This way we will develop a so-called “bullet-proof” mentality: a never-give-up attitude, logical thinking, a calm approach, confidence and increased emotional intelligence.

### Early days

- Most sales happen before prime time
- Gets you buzzing for the day, and you are more likely to stay focused as you had early sales
- Does not test your attitude or stamina
- Anyone can perform on that day

### Steady days

- A typical, normal day where the sales come consistently throughout the day
- Does not really test us, as the sales happen regularly

### Late days

- This is when the sales happen towards the end of the day
- On those days our attitude is tested
- This is when we learn the most about ourselves
- This is when we understand how important setting goals is, and how it allows us to stay focused
- These days help us develop a strong mentality, determination, persistence, and how to stay positive
- These days prove that the L.O.A. and following the systems works
- These days are the best “teachers”

Any of these scenarios could happen on any given day. It's how we react to it that will determine how soon we become consistent at sales, i.e. not giving up on a day when late sales are occurring. We never know where a sale is: it could be the first person we speak to or the last person of the day.

> The difference between a top performer and an average performer is how well they understand the different days, territories and customers, and how well they know themselves, to allow themselves to think logically and get the desired results despite any challenges.

title: Saving Time in the Field
summary: How to create the right habits to save and make more time in the field.
body:
## What?

Time is money. We all have the same hours in a day, yet some of us use them efficiently and effectively, maximising the chances to succeed, and some waste a lot of time being distracted and disorganised.

## Why?

- Improves your averages and earnings in the field, because you are able to see more people
- As a new BA you need to see more people to gain more experience
- By seeing more people, you will become an expert and quicker at a sign-up
- Spending less time with negative people helps you keep your attitude

## How?

- Plan and organise maps, directions, territory and pairings before you leave the office: knowing your way to the field, knowing travel times, grabbing lunch together if needed
- Check everyone has their stuff before leaving: badge, branded clothing, call back trackers, merch, pens, lunch
- Always have spare pens, call back trackers and merch, to avoid frustrations
- Use the bathroom before leaving the office
- Have lunch packed and ready, so we are not making anyone wait
- Be the first one to leave the office
- The minute we arrive at the field, start straight away
- Within the first hour get to know your territory, types of customers, demographics and potential objections, and share tips with your sector
- Qualify early: don't waste time with non-qualifiers
- Spend time with the right people
- The 5-second rule: when we knock, count to 5 seconds and then go. It keeps us focused and creates a next-door mentality, and also allows the customer to get to the door
- Hustle between doors
- Take a deep breath on the doors to control our tone of voice
- Have short and proactive sector breaks. Don't waste time at the breaks: break your day down, have a snack and go back
- Avoid bad examples that waste time, i.e. sitting in the car, café or takeaway for no reason
- Maintain the same tempo and momentum, to spread your energy throughout the day and keep a great level of work ethic. Moving too fast will slow us down at the end of the day; moving too slow will make us complacent, and we will miss quality customers who are working shifts, or from home that day
- Mark off the call back tracker as we knock on the next door. Don't stop in the middle of the pavement marking off your last appointment
- Always go that “extra mile”: pitch till the end, to use your time effectively
- Set up call backs throughout the day and for the next day. Keep your call back tracker and try to re-walk it the next day
- Always watch someone on 10 doors to upskill yourself, and apply it after. It may seem like a waste of time, but it actually makes us better and stronger, which in reality saves us time
key_facts: Time is money: seeing more people improves your averages and your earnings
The 5-second rule: knock, count to 5 seconds, then go
Qualify early: don't waste time with non-qualifiers
Mark off the call back tracker as you knock on the next door
Have short and proactive sector breaks

1. **Have a positive ATTITUDE**  
   Thinking positively improves any situation and helps deal with challenges better. Let the way you think work for you, not against you. Your attitude is determined by the way in which you view events as they happen. This business is 99% attitude and 1% ability.

2. **Be RELIABLE**  
   Time management is essential for success. Being early gives us time to achieve our goals and prepares us for the unexpected. Punctuality is a reflection of your discipline and ambitions. Keep your word, so people can trust you and rely on you.

3. **Be PREPARED**  
   Always aim to put yourself one step ahead by being ready for any situation. Have a student mentality (Listen, Learn and Apply). Preparation is the key to success. Knowing what needs to be done and having your day planned allows things to go that much smoother.

4. **100% EFFORT**  
   This is your business, and you are affected directly by your actions, so make sure you benefit by putting in 100%. An extra 10% all the time and you will be surprised by what you can actually achieve. Remember: the more effort you put in, the more you get out. You are the catalyst of your business.

5. **Work your TERRITORY correctly**  
   Everyone has the potential to be a buyer. Do not pre-judge customers, as they may be the ones that purchase from you. Avoid pre-judging difficult territories on appearance or demographics, as they may be a gold mine for you if someone else has pre-judged before.

6. **Safeguard your ATTITUDE**  
   While starting with a positive attitude is very beneficial, being able to protect it is even more important. We are in control of what we think, so it is important to make the right decision and control your thought process.

7. **Know your GOALS and WHY**  
   Set yourself both long and short-term goals. Keep focused on your purpose and be clear about what you want to gain and achieve, then work out exactly how to achieve it. By pushing to hit your goals you will become accustomed to achieving success consistently.

8. **TAKE CONTROL**  
   Be confident! Take control of your own situation. The choice is yours: take control of your future. It allows you to progress quicker. Remember you are running your own business, so assume the role from the beginning. The way you dress, walk and talk should show and determine how ambitious you are.

title: Habits & Consistency
summary: How to build the right habits and make sales your second nature.
body:
## Building new habits

Habits account for about 40% of our behaviours on any given day. Understanding how to build new habits (and how your current ones work) is essential for making progress.

1. **Start with an incredibly small habit.**  
   Make it so easy you can't say no. Your motivation comes and goes, so pick a new habit that is easy enough that you don't need motivation to do it. That's why our coaching is a step-by-step approach, focusing on one thing at a time.

2. **Increase your habit in very small ways.**  
   1% improvements add up surprisingly fast. So do 1% declines. Rather than trying to do something amazing from the beginning, start small and gradually improve.

3. **As you build up, break habits into chunks.**  
   Working the day correctly? Split it into 3 laps. Trying to speak to 80 people in a day? Break it down into 12 people an hour to get there more easily.

4. **When you slip, get back on track quickly.**  
   Top performers make mistakes, commit errors and get off track just like everyone else. The difference is that they get back on track as quickly as possible. You just need to be consistent, not perfect. Focus on building the identity of someone who never misses a habit twice.

5. **Be patient. Stick to a pace you can sustain.**  
   Learning to be patient is perhaps the most critical skill of all. If you are adding daily sales to your business, start by focusing on one customer at a time. Do things you can sustain.

New habits should feel easy, especially in the beginning. If you stay consistent and continue increasing your habit, it will get strong enough and fast enough. It always does.

## Consistency

Consistency is all about our behaviour. The best way to ensure we engage in the right behaviour is to have a plan and follow it.

Anybody can have a great month or quarter, but those who can deliver month in, month out are the most valued performers.

1. Have a PLAN and stick to it
2. Prioritise effectively
3. Learn how to manage your emotions
4. Know your numbers
5. Eliminate distractions
6. Train yourself: self-awareness, self-regulation, self-discipline, self-motivation

### What?

- Learning the skill over and over again so it becomes a habit
- You need 21 days to allow a new skill to become a habit
- Everything you do: how you act, behave and perform
- Work ethic, attitude = performance
- Match what you say with your actions: be congruent

### Why?

- Your consistency sets the standards for your team
- More consistent earnings allow you to invest in your team and yourself
- Every business needs profit to grow: consistent profit = consistent growth

### How?

- Give 100% effort every day
- Follow all the systems
- Have an agenda and a goal every day
- Break them down and review them
- Be competitive with others and yourself
- Become proactive: get yourself continually retrained
- Aim to learn something NEW every day from a high roller
- Learn by watching it first. Do it together, and then do it by yourself
- Network with your organisation and other offices
- Be patient
- Practise, practise, practise until you master each skill

> You will become “consistently consistent” rather than “consistently inconsistent”.

Start with an incredibly small habit: make it so easy you can't say no
1% improvements add up surprisingly fast. So do 1% declines
Never miss a habit twice: be consistent, not perfect

title: Fails & Missing Sales
summary: What a fail is, why it happens, and how to avoid it.
body:
## What is a fail?

A fail is a sign-up that pays nothing.

- **Cancelled order:** the customer cancels before their first delivery
- **Delivery over 8 days:** the first delivery is more than 8 days away
- **No repeat weekly order created:** there are no repeat items on the order
- **Order below £5:** the repeat weekly order is under £5.00

## The main reasons it happens

### Cancelled order

- The customer has not received their first order, as they cancelled after we left or before their delivery
- The customer was not happy and had reasons to cancel
- We signed up a non-decision maker
- We have not done a thorough REHASH, therefore the customer wasn't fully aware of how to use the service and its benefits
- It was a rushed sale: the customer felt pressured and uncomfortable
- There was a poor rehash, or none at all, which leaves the customer confused, not fully informed and with no confidence in the product

### Delivery over 8 days

- The customer's delivery was set up by us more than 8 days away
- Their first delivery date wasn't suitable
- We pushed a date on them just to sign them up

### No repeat weekly order created

- The customer has not created a repeat weekly order, but ordered “one-off” products
- We did not support the customer in creating the order and explaining the service throughout
- We paid no attention to detail
- We did not check the customer's order before proceeding
- We rushed the customer in creating the order, just to give the discount to get a sale

### Order below £5

- The BA has created an order below £5.00
- The BA has created an order over £5.00, but only by including the delivery fee
- The customer has removed items from their order after we left, which resulted in the order value falling below £5.00
- We have not created value in the product
- The customer selected the wrong products, too little or too much: no real engagement from us to support their decision and how they can use the products long term

## Missing sales

A missing sale is where we signed the customer up without our discount code. The customer has been created, but is not assigned to our badge and name.

### How do missing sales happen?

- We didn't put our code in
- We used someone else's code
- Our code was not activated or working, and we did not communicate it with admin
- We rushed a sale

## Other reasons customers cancel

- The cost and competition
- Not understanding payments
- They do not want a delivery every week
- They didn't know it was a subscription
- Their partner did not want it
- They felt pressured

## How to avoid fails

- Make sure that you help the customer to create the weekly repeat order, and engage with them whilst they are selecting their products
- Always ask the customer to check their calendar to make sure the delivery date is good for them. Explain how the calendar works
- Paint the picture of them going shopping but not needing to think about milk or eggs, as we will get it sorted for them
- Always mention to the customer to complete their first full week of orders, and paint the long-term picture (amendments when on holidays, Xmas products, next year)
- Do not take control of the non-decision maker
- Do not ever rush the customer, and only sign up people who have time for us
- Leave the customer with a long-term impulse and always THANK them for their time, for supporting British farms and helping the environment, for making a difference and an impact for future generations
- Always do a thorough and detailed REHASH. Never skip it or assume that the customer knows everything
- Focus and attention to detail
- Be in control of what they are doing. Observe and help: when they are selecting products, when they are dropping the pin on the map. The only time you don't need to look is when they enter their password and payment details
- Don't rush the sale
- Use your code, not someone else's
- Double and triple check the order value. If you are engaging and acting as a guide to them, you should never miss putting the code in
- Create orders well over £5.00 before the delivery fee: we aim for an average of £13 or more
- As many items as possible have to be on the repeat weekly order
- Set the right delivery days for them
- Explain how their calendar works and remind them to complete their first full week of deliveries before they start amending their future orders
- Make sure they know how to add one-off products, so they think about adding products, not removing them
key_facts: A fail pays nothing
Fail: the customer cancels before their first delivery
Fail: the first delivery is more than 8 days away
Fail: the order is under £5
Fail: no repeat weekly order was created (one-off products only)
A missing sale is a sign-up without your code: the customer exists but is not assigned to your badge

title: Sign-Up Process

body:
## Before we start

Before we set up a new customer for a regular weekly order, we need to make sure of a few things:

- The customer must be over 18.
- They must have a valid method of payment (credit or debit card).
- The customer must be present throughout the sign-up process.

On top of the basics, you must also ensure:

- The customer is aware that Modern Milkman is a flexible subscription model, and that they can amend their orders after they complete their first week of deliveries.
- The customer is not using a traditional milkman. With us there are no cash payments, and they can't call to change an order.

> Do double check these points. If a customer has been signed up and the above has not been followed, the customer could lodge a complaint, and your sale could be deemed mis-sold or even fraudulent.

## Guiding customers through the sign-up process

It is crucial that we help our customers through the sign-up process, to ensure that we provide the highest level of customer care before, during and after the process is complete.

To access the sign-up process in the field, we use the handy QR code found on the back of the pitch card, for our customers to scan on their own mobile device. This takes the customer to The Modern Milkman sign-up page.

### What the customer should know before joining

- They will be charged for the first delivery on the day you set up a repeat weekly order with us.
- They must pay by card, and the card holder must be present.
- They will receive the same order in their 2nd week unless they amend the order.
- Future deliveries are billed 3 days in advance of the first delivery day of that week. Any additional repeat weekly orders will be billed immediately, and then added to the weekly billing cycle the following week.
- This three-day advance gives some leeway if a payment fails for any reason, such as the bank rejecting the payment. If this happens, Modern Milkman will try to take payment again over the three days leading up to delivery. If they still can't take payment, they will have to cancel the delivery.
- Every complete sale must have an order number.
- The customer will receive an email confirming the set-up of their account and their payment.

> Note: all Modern Milkman customers must have an active email address and phone number to register. Never set up an email account on behalf of the customer.

Once you have made the customer aware of these crucial points, have the customer enter their card details. Be sure never to handle a customer's credit card yourself! Next step: place the order, and the sign-up process is complete.

## On the phone: the sign-up script

*(Relate whilst they are getting their phone and going on the App Store or Play Store.)*

> So what I've been doing for some of your neighbours today is helping them create an account. You choose the products you normally use in your weekly shop, like your milk, eggs, bread and fruit juice. I'll then put in my promo code, which will secure you your spot on the round with the milkman. And as a thank you, you get a discount for 2 weeks.

### The 10 steps

1. Go on The Modern Milkman website
2. Get started
3. Customer details
4. Drop the pin for deliveries
5. Home page welcome
6. Creating the repeat weekly order
7. APPLY PROMO CODE
8. Delivery instructions
9. Payment
10. Receipt number (8-digit code)

### Before you move on

- Explain payments
- Show how to manage regular orders
- Explain the cut-off time (8pm the night before delivery)
- Delivery is always on the doorstep by 7:30am
- Remind them to leave the empty bottles out
- Keep an eye out for future products
- Remember to recommend friends and family to join our milk round and get extra discounts

title: Creating the Order
summary: How to create value in the product and build the perfect repeat weekly order.
body:
## Building a regular weekly order

**When:** as soon as the customer has put in their details and is on the product page. Remember: you are the expert, and you need to guide them through the process to ensure the best customer experience.

**Why:** it ensures that the customer is receiving what they want and need, which means they don't need to constantly go on their app, which means it becomes convenient and helps customer retention.

### Capturing the order before getting to the product page

1. “How much milk do you go through in a week? Great, and which milk do you normally get? Whole, skimmed or semi-skimmed? Perfect...”
2. “Do you drink juices? Great, which one is your favourite that you use regularly? And how many litres would you use in a week? Yeah... I'm guessing you would be happy to get them delivered in glass bottles as well?”
3. “Do you use eggs? Great, we do farm-fresh, free range eggs. How many eggs do you go through in a week? Great, I'm guessing you would be happy to get them delivered fresh from the farm?”
4. “And how about bread? Great, we deliver white and wholemeal bloomers and our special sourdough too. Do you usually use wholemeal or white bread? Do you like sourdough? Great, I'm assuming you would be happy to get them freshly delivered alongside your milk and eggs?”

### The six steps

1. **Start with the milk**
2. **Help advise the customer** on how best to spread their order over the 3 different delivery days
3. **Move on to the orange or apple juice:** “What days are best for you?”
4. **Eggs:** “Would you normally have them during the week, or more at the weekend?”
5. **Treats or bread:** “Would you like these regularly or just occasionally?”
6. **“Let me show you what else we do.** Do you think there are any of these you would use regularly?”

> TOP TIPS: Act like a waiter taking an order. Get customers telling you what they want. Always ask: MILK / EGGS / BREAD / JUICE?

### Once the regular order is set up

- Explain how to amend the regular orders: “If you find on a regular basis you are using more, or less, than what we have set up, this is how you change the regular orders.”
- “If you want to add something on as a treat, or just on the odd occasion, this is how to order a one-off.”

## How to fill up the basket

> “For 6 pints... Would it be ok if we delivered 2 on Tuesday, 2 on Thursday and 2 on Saturday? Just to keep it fresher and not fill your fridge too much. Is that ok?”

> “For 12 eggs... Would you rather get all the eggs delivered on 1 day, or spread them out over the week to get them fresher?”

**Suggest. Advise. Guide.** “Is that ok?” · “Would that work for you?” · “Are you happy with that?”

- Suggest days and ask for agreement
- Indifference is key
- The customer makes the decision
- Subtle agreements
- Right customers and right amounts
- Product knowledge: use the product!

### Common mistakes

- Leaving it till the basket to upsell (too late)
- Allowing them to start with less than they use
- Not asking enough questions to create interest in other products
- Making the customer feel rushed or forced
- Rushing with the discounts just to sign a customer

## Creating value

Creating value in the products results in strong customer loyalty. It is a way to build strong bonds and solid relationships with customers in the long term.

### Why?

- The more value we give to the product, the more the customer will value it
- It builds more loyal customers for the long term
- Discounts may change
- Price may change
- Product may change

### How?

- Be sold on the product yourself: order it, taste it, understand it
- Connect with your customers to understand their needs
- Ask questions to identify their problems and help to solve them
- Become a master of G.I.F.T.S and USPs
- Show customers the benefits of using Modern Milkman products and services
- Use a pitch card to create a picture
- Speak with confidence, clarity and conviction
- Get strong agreement on the full price: the discount is just a bonus
- Speak with decision makers and sign up the right people

## The order value

| Tier | The customer's repeat weekly order |
| --- | --- |
| Silver | £5.00 to £9.99 |
| Gold | £10.00 or more |

The bigger the order value:

- The more problems we solve for the customer
- The more they benefit
- The longer they stay using The Modern Milkman
- The more plastic is saved
- The more efficient the round

To work out the order value, take the value of all the weekly repeat items in the basket, minus the delivery fee. We aim for an average of £13 or more.

title: Step 5: Rehash

body:
> STEP 5 · REHASH — Always invest time into doing a great consolidation, to ensure the quality of the sale and the customer's satisfaction.

## Step by step

1. **How to manage the app**  
   Advise the customer to download the app · explain each section of the app · show how to add one-offs and future products · explain the delivery calendar

2. **Weekly repeat order**  
   Help them create weekly repeat orders · explain the self-managed subscription · explain deliveries, deadlines and payments

3. **Leaflet & pop quiz**  
   Fill in the leaflet for them and leave a personal message · remind them of discounts and gifts for recommending friends · ask the customer if they have any questions for you · before leaving, ask questions to ensure their understanding

4. **Thank you**  
   Always thank customers for their time, to create a long-term relationship · thank them for supporting our British farms and helping the environment by using glass bottles with us · leave them with a positive long-term impact

> FINAL TIPS: Great quality and customer service is the key to long-term success. Always leave the customer on a positive note. Never skip or rush the consolidation. Spend quality time with each customer.

## The rehash script

### After-sale care

Before we leave the customer we should not only answer any questions they may have, but also walk them through and ensure they understand how the service will work for them moving forward. This is the time the customer really gets excited about their purchase and all the benefits that come along with using Modern Milkman!

> Thanks for signing up with us today! Before I go, I'd just like to show you a few things on the app, just so I know you're fully confident with everything.

### The app

**Picture**

> The first thing: let's take a picture of your doorstep, just so that your milkman can deliver your products to where you want them. If you just go on My Account, then the + button.

**Your next delivery**

> So, if you tap on this arrow here: this is where you can see your repeat orders. You can then tap on the date, and it'll show you what you're getting on that date! If you need to pause it on holidays, or skip it here and there, you can do that too.

**Product page**

> If you need to add anything extra, tap on any of the products and you'll have two options. You can either set it up as a repeat order to come weekly, or you can also get it as a one-time order: pick the date, and we'll deliver it to you just the once.

> You can only get a one-time order on a day that you already get a repeat order on, so for you it would be on ⟦text "their delivery days"⟧. And if you ever added another regular order on another day, you could use that for one-time orders too.

> Any questions about anything on the app? Great, we do have a help & support section if you need anything.

### The welcome leaflet

> The other thing I've got for you is this welcome leaflet.

*(Front page)*

> If you just go onto your camera and scan this QR code, we've put everything online just so we don't have to print more paper, to make it more sustainable.

> This is a page with lots of information about our service, the products, and where they're sourced from. We only ever use our British, independent farms, dairies and suppliers, so we aim to support the national little guys as opposed to the international big chains. It means more of the money you spend goes directly to these guys, which helps them and their businesses operate more sustainably and ethically. Hopefully, you agree it's a better way of shopping. *(nod)*

> It's also got some handy tips and FAQs to get the best out of our service. Please have a read of this when you're inside, and you get to keep this welcome leaflet as well.

*(Back page)*

> This shows you some details about your delivery and the products you've ordered.

### The pop quiz

> Now just before I go, I've got a little POP QUIZ for you, just to make sure I've done my job properly. Are you ready?

- When's your first delivery? *(Write the day of the first delivery on the leaflet.)*
- What are your delivery days?
- What's the latest you can make changes to your order by?
- What's your payment day? *(Write the payment date for them.)*
- What's your milkman's name?
- Apart from me knocking, what's the main reason you got involved?

### Closing statements

> Thanks again so much, you're a legend!

> The last thing: your discount will only last for the next 2 weeks. Here is how to take FULL ADVANTAGE of the service in your first 4 weeks.

> **Week 1:** This is for you to see the quality of the products.

> **Week 2:** This is for you to review the quantities that you're getting, so if you need more or less you can adjust that in your second week.

> **Week 3:** Hopefully you start to see the convenience of the service, and you notice you go down to the shops a lot less.

> **Week 4:** You'll start to notice a lot less plastic in your recycling, and start to see the difference you're making to the single-use plastic problem in the world.

> Also, in your 4th week, we'd love for you to review our service and let us know how much plastic you've helped save with us.

> Thank you so much for supporting. It makes a big difference to the farmers and the environment. We'll be around again in the next 6–8 weeks, so let us know how you've got on with the service! Hope you enjoy it.

## The mentality behind quality and rehash

### Why?

- Adopt the attitude that only half of your money is earnt from the customer's sign-up, and that the other half is earnt from consolidating the sale. This will lower your customer cancellations
- Many cancellations can be pre-empted and avoided by performing a thorough consolidation with a customer
- It is essential that all BAs and Leaders understand why a good consolidation is IMPORTANT: not only how to do it, but how to relay and show this information to others

### How?

- Take the customer through the leaflet
- Explain what happens next
- Highlight the main benefits of signing up. It will help them easily explain it to their partners, family and friends. They won't ever cancel if they understand everything
- Write down the small steps of what will happen next, so the customer knows
- Relate before you leave the customer

### The importance of a strong rehash

The first 4 steps only make up part of a sale. A weak rehash, or none, leaves that customer with doubts and unanswered questions, which means the customer might easily change their mind at any point after you have left their house.

**Why?**

- Leaves the customer with a long-term impulse
- You get fewer cancellations
- You get more week 4 payments
- Verifies the customer's understanding

**How?**

- Only ever sign the decision maker
- Spend plenty of time being thorough with your rehash
- Use sales collateral to help paint pictures
- Use long-term impulses, and help the customer envision themselves benefiting for years to come
- Ask the customer what questions they have
- Have questions ready to test the customer's understanding
- Show them the contact details in case they have any questions
- Re-sell the benefits and make it specific to them
- Leave your name: this makes it more personal

> TIPS: Finish each sale with a detailed REHASH to ensure customers know everything before we leave. Thank them and talk into the future. Show them how to use the app: customers who use the app stay long term.

## The customer experience

The customer experience starts with us, the Brand Ambassadors. Our friendliness, informativeness and infectious energy may be the customer's first experience of The Modern Milkman brand, so it's important to get it right. Members of the public will see us as the face of The Modern Milkman. We all have a responsibility to uphold the image of the brand at all times. The client puts trust in us and our customer service, so it's important our actions and behaviours create a positive image for the brand.

- Be too pushy
- Mislead or lie to customers
- Be rude or aggressive. Any form of unprofessional conduct (making offensive comments to customers, venue staff or members of the public) will not be tolerated
- Swear, or use inappropriate or dishonest ice breakers. A poor first impression can very often lead to a complaint and a future customer loss
- Wear your badge outside of working hours
- Give customers the impression you are representing a different company
- Be sarcastic or patronising towards customers
- Commit fraudulent activity or write incorrect customer details
- Drop customers' names or breach confidentiality

- Physically handle a customer's credit or debit card during the sale
- Smoke, eat or drink alcohol whilst wearing branded clothing
- Go inside someone's home without an invitation, or ask to use a customer's bathroom or toilet
- Promote any product or service other than The Modern Milkman. This includes making any form of disparaging remarks relating to another product, service or competitor
- Engage with social media as a representative of The Modern Milkman under any circumstances without first receiving permission

## DOs

- Be polite and courteous, and display a professional manner at all times
- Branded clothing must be worn in accordance with The Modern Milkman guidelines
- Identification must be worn and visible at all times
- Leave every customer on a positive note
- Make it clear whom you are representing
- Take extra time with vulnerable customers
- Always thank the customers for their time, even if they don't sign up

title: Mis-Selling & Fraud
summary: Under no circumstances can a Modern Milkman subscription be mis-sold.
body:
## Mis-selling explained

Under no circumstances can a Modern Milkman subscription be mis-sold. Examples of mis-selling include, but are not limited to:

- Misleading or taking unfair advantage of any person, such as minors (customers must be aged 18 or over), elderly or vulnerable customers, people who do not speak English, or people who are hearing impaired or mentally ill. If you aren't sure, don't engage in a customer transaction. Rather, leave the customer on a positive note and refer them to the website
- Failing to accurately describe the features of the product, including the price and the mechanics of the subscription model
- Fraudulently imitating a customer, fabricating false details, or taking a customer's details
- Making changes to a customer's account with or without their permission (i.e. removing items from their order for them)
- Signing up existing customers
- Creating multiple subscriptions within one household
- Making recommendations to pause a customer's account in an attempt to close a sale
- Selling The Modern Milkman as a “one-off” delivery

## Fraudulent subscriptions

Subscriptions that have been created under dishonest means are deemed “fraudulent” by The Modern Milkman. They take these sign-ups very seriously: they can create a poor product and brand experience, affect both the marketing company and The Modern Milkman financially, and promote a negative brand image.

Some specific examples of this are:

- Signing up an already existing customer. This includes the customer using alternative details to create a new account, or pausing their existing account whilst setting up a new account
- The BA offering to pay for the customer's first order themselves, and encouraging them to update their payment details
- Suggesting or recommending that customers pause multiple weeks on their account, or that they do this themselves at home. Instead, our policy is to show the customer how to skip a week if they are away or don't want a delivery that day, but to leave all weeks active on their account

## No pushy and aggressive sales

The Modern Milkman is sensitive when it comes to pushy and aggressive sales techniques, as this can severely damage the image of the brand in multiple ways.

We would consider this behaviour:

- Continuing to push a customer towards signing up when they have made clear that they are not interested or will not be signing up

Modern Milkman will investigate any complaints received on a case-by-case basis, passing these on to the marketing company for a statement or response. If the BA is deemed to be in breach of this, they will be referred to the marketing company's own code of conduct where applicable, or asked to be removed from the campaign in severe cases.
key_facts: Never mislead or take unfair advantage of anyone: only sign up people aged 18 or over who fully understand the subscription
Accurately describe the product, the price and how the subscription works
Never make changes to a customer's account, with or without their permission
Never sign up existing customers, or create more than one subscription in a household
Never sell The Modern Milkman as a 'one-off' delivery, or recommend pausing an account to close a sale
Never offer to pay for a customer's first order

title: Common Issues
summary: How to deal with obstacles and remain calm.
body:
## 1 · App or website not working

- Report it to the Sector Leader and the Owner, so they can inform the supplier, who will investigate with the client
- Remain calm: most tech issues are fixable in a matter of time
- Set up good call backs

| Problem | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Menu button not working | Use the basket to ADD more products, or go to My Account and press HOME |
| Order value not showing the discounted price | Explain to the customer that it still charges them the discounted price. It shows after they've added the payment card |
| It says “Sign up” at the top of the page and pressing the back button logs out | DON'T press the back button. Use the web and press back at the bottom to return to the previous page, or use My Account, then Home, to return |
| Delivery days not showing, or specific days missing | Explain to the customer that we are so popular the van is full on those days, so they can only use the available days. Check back later for more days after receiving the first order |
| Can't access help and support | Explain to the customer how to contact The Modern Milkman in the future, or show them on our own app |
| Logged out after sign-up, and logging back in as an existing customer | Switch to the app or site and LOG back IN. If it is not working, use an alternative number |
| Infinite loading after payment | Half close the app so it shows the open app tiles. Don't close it: just click back on it again and the loading should stop |

## 2 · Dealing with vulnerability

- We should take all reasonable steps to treat all customers fairly and enable them to make informed decisions about the products we are representing
- We should respect any potential customers who may require additional care or support, or may be in a vulnerable circumstance, and politely advise them to check us online
- We must not sign up any customers that show any signs of vulnerability

## 3 · No-cold-calling zones

If we are advised by someone that we are in a no-cold-calling zone (NCCZ), we must:

- Politely inform the customer you were not aware of this, and check with your coach
- Leave the immediate vicinity straight away, to allow the area to be checked and to avoid further issues
- Inform your coach and the Owner immediately. If the area is confirmed as an NCCZ, we will be requested to move to a sector nearby. If the area is confirmed not to be an NCCZ then we may continue in this sector. If any further complaints are made, we should leave the area immediately and advise the Owner to inform the client

## 4 · Lost or misplaced badges

In the event of losing the client ID badge, we must:

- Immediately stop. We cannot engage, under any circumstances, with a customer or potential customer without a valid ID badge
- Advise your Leader that you do not have an ID badge with you
- Return to the office, report the missing badge, and request a replacement

title: Best Practices
summary: General campaign tips to achieve high quality.
body:
- Always invest time into doing a good consolidation with the customer. If the customer has questions after we leave, they will probably cancel.

- During the sales process, sell at the full price and give analogies compared to the full price. This will ensure the customer stays after the promotions have gone.

- Sell yourself on the product. Try out the products and you will realise what great value we are offering at the full price.

- Remind the customer of the problems that we are solving for them. It's not just milk that we are selling, but a new way of life for the customer.

- Ask the customer questions to make sure they understand how it works.

- Talk long term: remind them to pause when on summer holidays next year, or at Xmas, so it is far in the future. Ask them what plans they have, any holidays planned, where they are going and how long for, so you can paint the picture in their head.

- Show them how to select “one-off” products, and also how the delivery calendar and payments work.

- Make sure that they are getting products that they want, need and are excited about, and recommend a few to try in the future.

- During the sales process and at the end, tell the customers to use us for the next 4 or 5 weeks, to give us a real chance, and to spread the word for extra discounts.

- Don't say: “try it out for 1 week”, “give it a go”, “if you don't like us, you can always cancel”. This doesn't show our confidence in the product and promotes short-term thinking. Instead say: we know you are going to love us and use us forever.

- Know your product. Do you know what products we are offering other than milk and eggs? Choose a few products that you are excited about and recommend them to the customers, so you can paint the picture and get them excited.

- Ask your customer the right questions. Telling a customer that they need less than they use, and can add products later, will only end in cancellation, or can even lead to a complaint. Ask politely about the age of the children, how much milk they drink, and whether they drink the same milk as the parents.

- Tell the customer that if they introduce friends and family, they will get a discount, and their friends will get one as a credit to use for future orders. If they know enough people, they may never pay the full price. Tell them to use both weeks of their discount, and to start recommending friends after that to get more discounts long term.

title: How to Use the COD

body:
## Cycle of Development

### The Proof Ladder

#### K · Know

Can explain it simply

#### D · Do

Can execute it effectively in the office

#### D · Deliver

Hits the standard under pressure in the field

#### T · Teach

Can transfer it to others

#### S · Systemise

Following proven systems to create independent examples of WGLL

### The 4 Pillars

#### Commercial Craft

The technical skills of the role. How you execute the sign up process, engage customers, handle questions, close confidently, and maintain quality under pressure. This is the foundation of performance.

#### Self Leadership

How you manage yourself. Your reliability, planning, resilience, emotional regulation, and ownership of your own results and development. No one can build this for you.

#### People Leadership

How you show up for and influence others. From following and enforcing standards as a BA, to coaching, developing, and holding a team accountable as a Leader.

#### Digital & Data

How you use numbers and systems. Accurate data submission, using KPIs to self-coach, tracking team performance, and making decisions driven by evidence, not feelings.

### Weekly Rhythm

- Choose the next stage and agree the outcomes and proof required
- Coach on the 4 pillars: Commercial Craft, Self Leadership, People Leadership, Digital & Data
- Review weekly: numbers, behaviour, evidence, decisions
- Drives results that are specific, owned and evidenced
- Progression only happens when evidence is shown and standards are consistently met
- Implement what good looks like (WGLL)

### Non-negotiables

- Standards are measured, owned and enforced with a consequence
- Data discipline: decisions are driven by numbers and evidence, not emotion
- Progression is a result of disciplined independence

title: Coaching Skills
summary: Effective tips for everyday coaching, and the four stages of learning.
body:
## What is coaching?

Coaching has traditionally been associated with sports. Every top athlete has a coach. In the last few years, coaching has become applicable in every area: in business and in every aspect of life.

Coaching is a process where a coach supports an individual to make a change, learn something new or achieve their goals. In coaching, fundamentally, the coach is helping the individual to improve their own performance: in other words, helping them to learn. Coaching builds awareness, empowers choice and leads to change.

> Coaching is unlocking a person's potential to maximise their own performance. It is helping them to learn rather than teaching them.

## What is a coach?

A coach is someone who takes on a supportive and guiding role to help people reach their full potential. Through coaching, they give people the resources and encouragement they need to excel by:

- Evaluating people's performance
- Identifying performance-related goals and objectives
- Providing ongoing feedback about areas of improvement and suggesting skills to learn
- Monitoring progress in achieving those goals
- Offering resources and knowledge to improve those skills

### The skills of a great coach and a great student

Both roles require mutual respect, a common learning and progression goal, and teamwork. To achieve the best results on both sides, have an honest chat about the student's goals and the coach's objectives.

`Listening` `Questioning` `Building rapport` `Empathising` `Summarising & reflecting` `Unlocking limiting beliefs` `Staying focused` `Being non-judgemental & open-minded` `Giving constructive feedback` `Resisting the temptation to tell`

> In business and in life, relationships define our progression, our success and even our happiness. As coaches, we have a responsibility to open the channels to better communication.

## The competency cycle

The four stages of competence are a learning model of the psychological states of individuals going through the progression from incompetence to competence for a certain skill.

1. **Unconscious incompetence**  
   You don't know that you don't know about something. A good example would be a child who has never seen a bicycle.

2. **Conscious incompetence**  
   You have become aware that you lack a particular skill. An example might be the child who has seen other children riding bicycles, and therefore wishes to learn.

3. **Conscious competence**  
   You have learned how to do something, but you still need to think about it in order to do it. An example would be the child who can ride a bicycle but falls off if they stop watching where they are going.

4. **Unconscious competence**  
   You have learned how to do something so well that it has become hard-wired into your brain. You no longer have to think about how you do it, but just do it.

Coaches need to identify the stage an individual is at, to use the right sort of language and coaching to help them move to the next stage. After all, it's difficult to try to improve a skill if you don't know that you lack it.

## Tips for first-time coaches

### Get to know your students

- 100% chat
- Expectation of the relationship
- Goal finding
- Tailoring the coaching

### Plan your sessions

- Be organised and prepared
- Notes, handouts, tools
- Set objectives and goals
- Review and recap the session

### Never stop learning

- Study sales, the product, the industry and yourself
- Read books, listen to podcasts

### Observe other coaches

- Observe other coaches' style
- Watch the delivery of the sessions, i.e. body language and tone of voice
- Learn from their experience
- Ask for tips and advice

### Keep it simple

- Don't overcomplicate the impacts and sessions
- Be clear with the message
- Deliver relevant content
- Concise but thorough
- Easy to take notes

### Be aware of learning styles

Everyone is different; therefore, we learn differently. Be aware of the way people learn and adapt your sessions so everyone can learn: kinesthetic, auditory, visual.

### Make it fun and creative

- Educate and motivate through learning
- Inspire the change and encourage improvements
- Balance between intensity and fun
- Be unique and find your way of coaching

### Have standards and give advice

- Your image and preparation
- Speak from the heart and experience
- Share your mistakes, ups and downs, examples and best tips
- Always aim to make your students better
key_facts: Coaching is unlocking a person's potential to maximise their own performance: helping them to learn rather than teaching them
Skills: listening, questioning, building rapport, empathising, summarising and reflecting, giving constructive feedback
The competency cycle: unconscious incompetence → conscious incompetence → conscious competence → unconscious competence

title: Running Impacts
summary: How to make a difference and influence people.
body:
## What is an impact?

An IMPACT is a topic that is designed to make a difference in a Brand Ambassador's skillset. Impacts should be short and simple but thorough, clear and to the point, so they are easy to learn and remember.

### When?

- Anytime, anywhere, whenever necessary. They should be a big part of the Primetime you spend with people in the mornings and evenings. The more we coach people in the office through impacts, the less time we will need to spend re-educating them in the field
- Social meetings, i.e. breakfasts, dinners, BBQs: we can educate people in any setting
- Every day in the meeting room
- Whilst travelling to the field or during the breaks (as appropriate)

### How?

- Impacts can be as long or as short, as big or as small, as they need to be to get your point across
- Sales impacts should be quite short and to the point, interesting and fun, to make learning easier
- Engage with the audience and get them involved
- A whiteboard and marker in the office
- A pen and paper, or the COD stages, if away from the office

### Points to watch for

- If you have quite a large group, ensure new people are not hidden at the back, unable to hear or participate
- Eye contact is important, as when you pitch a customer. Do not turn your back on the group
- You should talk to the group, not at the group. Remember you were there once too
- Write clearly when using the whiteboard (props are also great to use)
- Speak clearly, be confident and enjoy!
- Make it a fun and interactive activity by asking lots of questions and getting them to participate

### Repetition

> “Repetition is the mother of skill.”

Impacts should be repeated as many times as required for the person to learn and apply them. Some students need to be on the same impact 10 times; some will pick it up after 3 impacts. Keep running the topics until your students can apply them independently. Always ask students to take good notes, so they can refer to them at a later time.

### Participation

Impacts should actively involve as many people as possible. Encourage people to talk, trigger their thinking and educate on taking notes.

### Assess

Always assess participants' understanding by getting them to display their skills, check their notes and recap what they've learnt. Ask questions and get people to practise scenarios in small groups or pairs.

## How to prepare yourself to run great impacts

Creating the right standards and communicating the expectations before running any impact is essential to becoming a successful coach. It is crucial that every participant is taking notes, and that you, as a coach, deliver great content and a clear message that's easy to remember. That's called CREATING AN IMPACT on someone and MAKING A DIFFERENCE.

### What you need to run a great impact

- A plan
- Notes to back yourself up
- A board marker (and a spare)
- Extra pens, to support your audience with note-taking
- Image
- A whiteboard (if needed for your impact)
- Knowledge on the topic
- Confidence
- Systems
- Results, for credibility and respect

### What each impact should involve

- Detailed content
- A clear, simple message
- A practical part, where you're practising what you've just learnt
- A recap, to assess students' understanding

### How to prepare

1. **1st time:** take notes and learn the content
2. **2nd time:** take extra notes and refresh yourself on the topic
3. **3rd time:** observe the delivery of the impact, focusing on body language and tone of voice
4. **4th time:** practise the impact on your colleague or coach and ask for their feedback
5. **5th time:** run it for people and ask your coach to watch it for feedback

Keep watching different coaches, and run impacts every day for different people to get better.

### Ideas for creative impacts and coaching sessions

`Game` `Group activity or exercise` `Competition` `Quiz or test` `Case study` `Impact cards` `Role play` `Open forum` `Q&A` `Brainstorming session`

title: Presentation Skills
summary: To give you confidence as a coach and to help you engage the audience.
body:
## Body language

### Face and hands

- Always make eye contact and look at all of your participants. Do not stare at them, but do make an effort to appear to speak to each and every person present
- Use facial expressions and gestures that match your words
- Speak to and engage those that are the furthest from you
- No playing with markers, touching your head, crossing your legs or arms, or hands in pockets

### Posture

- Maintain good posture. It helps to project your voice better and to look more confident
- Change your posture or position when highlighting a new point

### Positioning

- When standing at the front of the room, plant your feet and do not shift your weight, and avoid pacing back and forth on the same spot
- Be aware that sitting changes the tone and makes the atmosphere informal. Only use it when coaching small groups, when everyone can hear and see you
- Never have your back to the group (or as little as possible if you are writing on a board)

## Voice

### Volume, pitch and pauses

- Project your voice!
- Change the volume and pitch of your voice to add emphasis. If you need to, just ask the people at the back if they can hear you okay
- Pause to emphasise something important. Pauses are also useful to give time to reflect, and for you to observe participants
- Do not be afraid of silence!

### Fillers and elocution

Fillers are the words we unconsciously use to try and fill in between the things we are meant to say. Common fillers include “ah”, “err”, “ok”, “like”, “um” and “right then”.

- Try to avoid too many fillers (record yourself and play it back to hear if you are using too many)
- Do not rush the end of sentences
- Use an informal tone of voice to sound warm and friendly, but be professional

## Space

- Move around among participants
- Move around the room, looking first at one group, then another
- Do not neglect any section of the room
- Never sit behind a desk. For the most part, you should be standing when presenting

## Extra tips

- **Be concise.** Do not go on and on about something and be too repetitive. You can lose the attention of your audience
- **Be careful with jargon.** Make sure you are speaking with your audience in mind
- **Practise.** The best presenters are the best because of one key reason: they practise
- **Watch great presenters.** Observe the pauses at key moments, the way they move, the change of intonation for emphasis, the way they use their hands, and their facial expressions
- **Show enthusiasm!** If you are not interested in the topic you are coaching, you won't keep your audience engaged. Smiling and being happy is infectious!

> KEY TIP: Remember it all simply comes down to practice! The more times you run through your session, the smoother and more fluent you will become.

title: Role Play & Pitch Doctor
summary: How to practise effectively, and how to help someone find what to improve in their pitch.
body:
## Role playing

Role play is an interactive method used to practise conversations with potential customers, using real-life scenarios, tough examples and challenging situations, so the students can learn how to think for themselves in the field and help customers with their queries.

### Why use role play?

- Stimulates the brain to find solutions
- Builds confidence and fluency in your conversations
- Improves your skills and selling techniques
- Helps you become independent and think for yourself in the real world
- Makes you solution-orientated, so you can deal with any objection, query or situation

### When?

- In the morning sales coaching sessions
- On the way to the field
- In between doors in the field, if necessary, to polish the script

### Who?

Everyone: Owners, Assistant Owners, all Leaders and BAs.

### Effective role playing to build confidence

- Focus on one area at a time. Practise that part until fluency is achieved
- Use the 10/10/10 rule: 10 times Introduction, 10 times Presentation, 10 times Short Story, and so on
- Listen more than talk
- Repetition is key: keep working on one section until you see the body language and the tone of voice improving
- Each time you see a small improvement, recognise it by mentioning it, high-fiving them, fist-bumping them. Use any form of recognition to encourage more practice and improvement
- Give honest and constructive feedback
- Ask how they feel and if they are ready to move on to the next part. If not, keep practising
- Once fluency is achieved, practise different scenarios and situations
- Demonstrate your own script and ask what they've learned from it, so they can spot areas to improve in themselves

### Setting expectations and learning goals

- Before starting any impact or role-playing exercise, have a goal of what you want the person you are coaching to learn and improve on, e.g. getting into the close, rehash, smiling more, qualifying, turning objections
- Follow up on the impact and the improvements in the field, and recap the learnings at the end of the day
- Break everyone's day down in the evening and use those KPIs to identify what students need to improve on the next day. Plan your impacts and role-play scenarios beforehand

## Pitch doctor

There is a misconception that once you learn your pitch you don't need to practise. Unfortunately, that's a myth. Mastering sales and becoming an all-round Brand Ambassador that can represent any brand requires constant coaching and practice, like in any sport.

Once we master something, sometimes we can't see our own faults or weaknesses, and this is when a coach or mentor plays a key role: helping us find those areas of weakness, guiding us to strengthen them, and practising to improve ourselves.

### Key points to look for

- Are we impulsing in the introduction?
- Are we taking control?
- Are we assuming the sale?
- Are we sizzling the deal?
- Are our impulses exciting enough?

Keep on practising with someone until the above is achieved and both coach and student have the confidence that it will be applied. Revisit the session the next day to see the improvements.

### How should it be delivered?

We all know the famous comment: it's not what you say, it's how you say it. When checking someone's pitch it is important to FOCUS on body language and tone of voice, as they equate to 93% of our conversations, when words are only 7%.

- **Tone of voice:** do regular checks to make sure you can be heard and the pace you are speaking at is not too fast
- **Fun:** make sure you are having fun when delivering sales coaching. The more fun the person is having, the more they will learn
- **Atmosphere:** make sure you are constantly building confidence, e.g. ask other Leaders in the room to listen to the person you are coaching, and prep the Leader to say how well they are doing
- **Time:** it is vital that you spend as long as it takes to coach sales. This may mean you will have to repeat the process more than once, until the person has fully understood it

### Remember

1. Everybody is different: some students will improve quickly, some will be slower. Be patient.
2. Practising with someone and helping them with their skillset makes you better and stronger.
3. The more you practise, the better you become. There is no magical script.
4. Practice builds confidence. Confidence creates results. Results give more confidence, and the circle of success repeats itself.
5. Education is a form of motivation: the more you learn, the better results you get and the hungrier you become to learn more. Stay humble.

title: Coaching the Pitch
summary: What to look out for when guiding someone through their 5 steps.
body:
## What to look out for

When coaching new Brand Ambassadors in the basic pitch, it's crucial that we pay attention not only to the words they are using, but how they are saying and delivering the message. Here are 10 things to observe when guiding someone through their 5 steps:

1. Fluency
2. Body language
3. Tone of voice
4. Pitch card
5. Buzz words
6. Relating
7. Impulsing
8. Clear and concise message
9. Close
10. Rehash

Once these points are educated and understood by the Brand Ambassador, it is just a matter of time for them to become competent, confident and independent in their sales conversations.

> TIP: Practise the 5 steps every day by picking sections that need polishing or areas that need strengthening. Repetition is the mother of all skill.

## Overcoming setbacks when coaching the 5 steps

1. **Do I need to use the same words? Can I change things around?**  
   We can use our own words and favourite buzz words; however, we need to be careful with certain terminology. There are certain messages that should not be missed, like introducing ourselves and where we are from, but as long as we stick to the 5 steps structure, we can use our own words. It's proven, it works, and it guarantees results.

2. **Can I add certain things?**  
   The 5 steps is constructed in a way that it has enough impulses to excite the customer about the product. Adding more information could kill the impulse and complicate the message the customer is receiving. People's attention span tends to be short, which is why it's crucial to have a pitch that is short and direct.

3. **Can I shorten it?**  
   Shortening the 5 steps won't have the same impact on the customer. However, if you forget certain messages in your conversation, carry on and help yourself with the pitch card and other branded materials, and eventually you will find your words. Make sure you hit the key points.

4. **What if I am not a smiley person?**  
   All it takes is practice, like with everything else. Smiling is the most important part of any customer service role.

5. **I don't feel comfortable practising in the office.**  
   Share your story, as learning sales can be uncomfortable at first for some, but with practice everything becomes easier.

6. **I already know my pitch.**  
   Perfect, let's go over it again to identify your strengths, so we can help other people. Our business is like any sport or language: if we stop coaching, eventually our skillset will become weaker. Rule of thumb: there is always room to improve.

7. **Do I need to use a pitch card?**  
   A pitch card is a tool that allows us to remember what to say next, gives us confidence, and is an amazing visual aid for the customer. It also creates brand awareness and credibility in our message. Top performers always advise using one.

8. **Do I need to be with my coach when in the field?**  
   The coach's responsibility is to guide and support us in our first days in the field. As we are representing huge brands, it is imperative that the first few days are guided, to ensure we follow the brand's promise and deliver the right message to our customers. It is all about being competent, confident and independent.

9. **I am better in the field. I say it differently.**  
   The coaching part allows us to get better before we go out into the real world. Remember: the better the coaching, the easier it is in the field.

10. **I am nervous practising with more experienced people.**  
    Share your story. At first, we were all nervous, but with time, practice and experience we all became great coaches. We need to feel uncomfortable to become comfortable. Experienced people are the best way to get better, as you are learning from the best examples, and they all mean the best for you.

11. **I don't know what I need to practise.**  
    No problem. Let's check your knowledge, 5 steps (pitch doctor) and KPIs, and we will be able to figure out what to work on.

12. **My coach's pitch and everyone else's is different.**  
    What you hear is not different to what we've all learnt. Everyone has a different style, uses words that suit them best, and adapts the conversation to the situation using all the systems we've learnt. What we hear is all the systems working in sync. It is called the Art of Selling.

13. **My pitch is the best in the office, so I don't need to practise.**  
    That's amazing. I would like to improve mine: can we role play, so I can learn from the best example in the office? I believe there is always something we can learn from each other.

title: Setting Up & Reviewing the Day
summary: For maximum performance and minimum problems, and ten questions that help you understand someone's day.
body:
## Setting the day up

### Before the office

- Wake up earlier, to prevent running late or rushing
- Put effort into your image. It is the first thing that people and customers notice. It helps your confidence and builds a great reputation
- Prepare your lunch the night before, or in the morning. Create the right habits that lead to success: save time, save money, eat well and healthily, always be prepared, don't make people wait
- Leave the house and arrive in the office early, to be prepared for the unexpected and remove all excuses from your day

### In the office

- Welcome everyone and get to know your colleagues
- Have a notebook and take good notes, so you can learn and refer to them in the future
- Be proactive and use your time effectively: have a plan
- Keep on improving and learning something new
- Attend all relevant workshops and coaching sessions, to increase your sales skillset and business knowledge
- Use quality time in PRIMETIME coaching others and learning too
- Set your sector up before going to the field, to ensure everyone knows what the plan for the day is, and create a sense of urgency

### On the way to the field

- Communicate sector goals and discuss everyone's individual goals for the day
- Remind everyone of their learning focus for the day, and give tips on working different territories, scenarios and customers, and adapting the introduction
- Have downtime with the team: get to know people personally and build meaningful relationships
- Share success stories and examples from around the UK and other countries
- Motivate your sector through education, stories, competition and mini challenges, to achieve maximum performance each day

### In the field

- Follow the systems and be the best example of the 8 steps
- Have a strategy in the field, to work the territory effectively and maximise your results
- Always look for solutions: there is always a solution to anything
- Set the pace by leading from the front, through your example, performance and results
- Support your sector with advice and tips. Let them watch and study you, to better themselves
- Always have a back-up plan if things don't go your way
- Be logical about your day. Use systems and your knowledge to control your thought process: self-analyse, self-regulate, self-discipline, self-motivate

### After the field

- Always break your day down with your coach, sector leader or any performer, to know exactly what you need to work on the next day
- Analyse your day based on your KPIs, to understand how you can improve the next day
- Set the plan for the next day: what are you learning tomorrow, who are you spending time with in Primetime, what are you coaching, what impacts are you attending or running
- Communicate your plan with your coach, and prepare yourself for the next day full of education (don't forget your notebook)
- Network and socialise with people before going home, so you can build strong relationships for the future

## Reviewing the day

At the end of each day, it is crucial to discuss how someone's day went, especially when they were not working with you that day. This coaching exercise will allow you to check on someone's mood, challenges, positives and proud moments. It also helps to find out what areas need improving, and whether there is anything that requires your attention.

1. **“Did you have fun today?”**  
   Allows you to check someone's attitude, mentality, approach and point of view.

2. **“What did you learn today?”**  
   Allows you to identify what someone has learnt that day, and who from. A day without learning is a day wasted.

3. **“What time did you leave for the territory?” “What time did you leave to come back?” “Did you stop for lunch?”**  
   Allows you to find out whether the sector was run properly, whether there was the right influence and leadership, and whether the right decisions were made.

4. **“What challenges did you face today?” “Anything that annoyed you that I can help with?”**  
   Allows you to find out if someone got frustrated with themselves, their sector or customers, and whether they've learnt how to safeguard their attitude. If it's sales related, it gives you a clear idea of what to coach to remove those frustrations: objections, taking control, hooklines.

5. **“If you could do today all over again, what would you do differently?”**  
   Allows us to check whether they feel they need help, and whether they know how to look for improvements and solutions or we should suggest them.

6. **“Is there anything you'd like me to help you with?”**  
   Let them guide you to where they feel they need help. If the student is not aware of what to work on, help them in the areas you identified after breaking their day down.

7. **“Who did you spend the day with?”**  
   Allows us to find out who worked with them that day, and if they used their field time effectively by not only selling but watching someone to learn too. Always get feedback on someone's day from the Leader they were working with, to prepare yourself for the next day.

8. **“At what time did your attitude get affected?”**  
   Allows us to see whether they are solution orientated, logical or emotional, and follow the 8 steps.

9. **“What type of territory did you work today?”**  
   Allows us to identify if someone has learned how to work every territory or needs help with it, what challenges they faced, and if they worked the territory correctly.

10. **“Did you get to speak to enough people?”**  
    Allows us to identify if someone followed the L.O.A. and worked the territory effectively. Compare their answer with their call back tracker, and give examples of how to improve.
key_facts: Before the office: wake up earlier, put effort into your image, prepare your lunch
On the way to the field: communicate sector goals and everyone's individual goals
After the field: always break your day down, and set the plan for the next day
