## The new Brand Ambassador's first full day

### Morning

- Office tour: where everything is and what parts of the office are allocated for what
- Explain: the systems · our responsibility to the client · the clients we're representing · the importance of wearing an ID badge · the office schedule: who runs what, and the role of the Administrator · the recognition! Why we recognise others' achievements: bells and gongs are part of the morning
- Build their confidence: explain that their first day is an experience, no pressure
- Set a goal for the day together, and explain how important it is to hit your goals
- Prepare them for challenges
- Follow the 8 steps, to build your reputation as a coach and a Leader from day 1
- Introduce them to the team and to other new people
- Introduce them to people who are performing well at the time
- Don't leave their side: the “VELCRO EFFECT”

### During the day

- Keep the conversation flowing: make them feel at ease
- Be enthusiastic about each sale
- Maintain a great attitude and show them how to overcome obstacles and objections
- Have them present to you. Get them pitching: practice makes perfect
- Let them watch you sell for the first half of the day. Build their confidence in you and themselves
- Show them how to work the territory correctly

### Evening

- Explain the purpose of returning to the office in the evening, and what will be discussed
- Congratulate them on a great first day and for giving it their all

## Days 2 to 6

The next few days should be a continuation of the coaching and education regarding the client and the sales process started on their first day.

1. Keep in close contact with your new team members until they become proficient in their sales presentation.
2. Although these are early days, new team members should be making sales with you.
3. Monitor their development and identify what encouragement and support they require.
4. Set up calls with other BAs within the group who are doing well. Show them how to network and how easy-going everyone is. If you want them to do well, then they must socialise with high performers.
5. Learn to work with them as a team. You must be prepared to give them 100%.
6. Show them how to be profitable. They need to learn this as soon as possible.
7. Sit down with them each night and review their day.
8. Coach them through the stages of the COD. Explain what an amazing tool this is and how it will help their development into a successful business person within the sales industry.
9. Set goals. Show new team members how important goal setting is and the correct way to do it. Set them too high and they will lose faith; too low and they won't put the effort in.

## Week 1 coaching plan

See **First 2 Weeks** for the day-by-day plan: induction, product knowledge, then the script, G.I.F.T.S, objections, closing and rehash across the first days in the field.

- Contacting all team members

| --- | --- |
| **Week 1 · COD 1** | Introduction to our business · product coaching · sales coaching · practical observation and application in the field · giving it 100% · being a great student · attending the Business Advancement Meeting · pass COD 1 · personally recruiting |

| **Week 3 · COD 3** | Consistency · preparing for advancement to leadership · example setting · passing COD 3 · observing how to coach new BAs · learning how to run sectors · mastering sales systems · watching how to run basic impacts · monthly goal planner |
| **Week 4 · COD 3+** | Developing into Leadership · observing coaching methods · coaching new BAs · week 1 coaching · mastering running sectors · running impacts for new people and others · visiting an office |
| **Week 5 · COD 3+** | Watching more impacts, focusing on body language, tone of voice and delivery · learning presentation skills · hosting new people · advancing Leaders · learning how to develop someone to Leadership · showing others how to network · team name and logo |

title: Social Selling
summary: How to think outside the box and maximise your income.
body:
## What's happening?

The Modern Milkman has provided us with codes to allow all Brand Ambassadors, regardless of what campaign they are in, to socially sell a Modern Milkman subscription.

Social selling Brand Ambassadors can sell to customers outside of the usual door-to-door field experience. They can do this in a social setting, in their network, with friends and family. They may also use the code on all their social media platforms: this could be a post, or a code at the end of a video. Feel free to get creative with this!

The code gives a new customer a discount on their first weeks as a Modern Milkman customer.

> Check the current social selling discount with the Owner before you quote it.

## What do I need to do?

For anybody already on the Modern Milkman door-to-door campaign, their social selling code is the same as their usual badge number but with the letter “R” in front.

Anyone who isn't on the Modern Milkman door-to-door campaign must contact their Owner, who will issue a code for each Brand Ambassador who wants one.

## Criteria

Due to the nature of social selling, the process can be much more informal than a usual sale. However, there are a few things that the client has asked us to abide by.

### For online and social media content

Avoid content relating to violence, politics, or anything of a sexual nature, drugs, alcohol, religion or anything generally illegal in nature.

### General

- There is no minimum subscription. This will be monitored.
- If you are in a different campaign, do not give this code to the customers you sign up there. This will cause brand confusion.
- Avoid using strong disparaging language against The Modern Milkman's competitors. “The Modern Milkman are the crème de la crème of milk companies” is a great post. Naming a competitor and saying their milk tastes awful is not ok.
- If using these codes you must agree that you will take down posts if directed to by Acwyre or the client.

Please consult the Owner if you think your post might be slightly “too edgy”.

## Payment

The office receives a weekly report from the client showing all the social selling for the previous week. These are added to your earnings summaries, along with a report showing which code achieved the sign-up.

- The fee for any social sale is **£10.00**.
- If anyone accidentally posts their regular door-to-door badge number, there will be no social selling fees paid on any customers that sign up using it.
key_facts: Social selling is a Modern Milkman subscription sold outside the door-to-door field: your network, friends and family, your social media

The fee for a social sale is £10.00

title: Understanding the Industry
summary: Subscriptions, plastic and recycling: facts worth knowing, and good conversation starters.
body:
## Subscriptions

### Why do people love subscriptions?

- Trendy, cool, futuristic
- A new way of living and shopping
- Flexible
- The customer is in total control: self-managed
- Easy to use, simple and straightforward
- Exciting and inspiring
- Convenient
- Fast deliveries
- New customer discounts, referral and loyalty programmes, vouchers, freebies
- Time saving and efficient
- Great value for money
- Makes our life easier and improves our lifestyle
- A variety of options and choice
- An opportunity to discover new products

### Why do people not use subscriptions?

- Scared of change
- Fear of the unknown
- Too complicated
- Used to their own old ways
- Busy with life
- Can't be bothered
- Lack of understanding
- Perception
- Too good to be true
- Procrastination
- Not knowing what's out there

### Why do businesses love subscriptions?

- A new customer base
- Brand reputation and awareness
- Better profitability
- Wider reach
- Easy to scale up
- An analysis tool: trends, behaviours, patterns
- Long-term, more loyal customers
- A new source of sales
- Online and social presence

## Plastic: did you know?

- One recycled bottle can save enough energy to light a 60W lightbulb for 6 hours
- 5 plastic bottles can create enough fibre to fill one ski jacket
- Almost every piece of plastic ever made still exists today
- It takes around 450 years for one plastic bottle to break down into the ground
- Half a trillion disposable cups are manufactured around the world annually. That's more than 70 disposable cups for every person on the planet every single year
- 80% of marine litter is plastic
- 300 million tons of plastic waste are produced every year
- 90% of the cost of bottled water is the bottle itself
- Between 500 billion and 1 trillion plastic bags are used worldwide annually
- The average time that a plastic bag is used for is 12 minutes, and then it takes up to a thousand years to decompose!
- Every time you wash synthetic fabrics, millions of microfibres are released into the water. They are too small to be filtered out, so they end up in our oceans
- The UK generates more plastic waste per person than any other country apart from the US
- 73% of all beach litter is plastic

> These facts are from the coaching booklet. Use them as conversation starters, and check a figure before you rely on it.

## Recycling mistakes

A good start-up conversation.

### 10 things you can't put in your household recycling

1. Sticky notes: the glue can't always be removed during the process
2. Toothpaste tubes: the aluminium and plastic are hard to separate
3. Drinking glasses: heat treated, so they do not melt at the same temperature as other glass items
4. Paper receipts: some are printed on shiny, thermal paper
5. Crisp packets: if the item springs back into shape after you have scrunched it up, then it shouldn't be recycled
6. Salad bags: they combine different types of plastic
7. Plastic sleeves on bottles
8. Crisp tubes: they combine 5 different materials
9. Cotton wool pads: 100% cotton can be added to your compost bin
10. Thick paper straws: difficult to collect separately to recycle

### 5 biggest recycling mistakes

1. It cannot be recycled if it is covered in food. Make sure you wash out all bottles, containers and tins
2. Plastic bottle tops should always be removed from the bottle
3. Disposable coffee cups have a thin layer of polyethylene which makes them waterproof, so they cannot be recycled
4. Never put your recycling in plastic bags, as it will go straight to landfill
5. Non-recyclable items include laminated pouches, crisp packets, plastic toys, cotton wool, toothpaste tubes and tissues

## Becoming great at sales

There are certain hard and soft sales skills you need to master to become incredible at sales.

| Soft skills | Hard skills |
| --- | --- |
| Relationship building | Product knowledge |
| Adaptability | Industry knowledge |
| Storytelling | Systems and processes: 5 steps, L.O.A., G.I.F.T.S, closing the deal, objection handling |
| Emotional intelligence | Using tools |
| Collaboration | Analysing data |
| Self-motivation and ambition | Coaching |
| Goal-orientated | Marketing research |
| Empathy | Social selling |
| Passion and enthusiasm | Customer service |
| Critical thinking and problem solving | Tech knowledge |
| Time management and organisation |  |
| Networking and communication skills |  |
| Growth mindset and active listening |  |

The skills we learn whilst studying sales are invaluable. Not only does this industry make us better and stronger, it also prepares us for the future: empathy, emotional intelligence, active listening, effective communication, confidence, adaptability, optimism, time management, public speaking, integrity, a growth mindset and customer service.

Why people don't use them: scared of change, fear of the unknown, a lack of understanding
It takes around 450 years for one plastic bottle to break down
The UK generates more plastic waste per person than any other country apart from the US
Sales skills become life skills: empathy, confidence, communication, time management
